The pattern is 70 characters. But this pattern has issues - the `(` and `)` in the alternatives would be interpreted as group delimiters. Let me escape them properly.

Actually, let me think about this differently. The pattern needs to match itself. Let me use a pattern where `.` matches any character, so the pattern can match itself regardless of the characters.

Let me use `(?:.)*` with a long subject. But the subject is the same as the pattern. So I need the pattern to be long.

Actually, let me think about this more carefully. The pattern `(?:.)*` would match any subject. So if I make the pattern `(?:.)*` followed by many characters, the `(?:.)*` would match the entire subject, and then the trailing characters would need to match. But there are no characters left after `(?:.)*` matches the entire subject.

Hmm, let me try a different approach. Let me use a pattern that matches itself and creates many frames.

Actually, let me reconsider. The key insight is that the pattern needs to create many frames. Each frame is created when the matcher enters a group with alternatives. So a pattern with many alternatives would create many frames.

But the pattern also needs to match the subject (which is the same as the pattern). So the pattern needs to match itself.

Let me try a pattern like `(?:a|b|c|...)*` where the alternatives include all the characters in the pattern. But the pattern itself contains `(`, `)`, `?`, `:`, `|`, `*`, etc. So the alternatives need to include these characters.

But `(` and `)` in the alternatives would be interpreted as group delimiters. I need to escape them: `\(` and `\)`.

Let me create a proper pattern:

`(?:a|b|c|d|e|f|g|h|i|j|k|l|m|n|o|p|q|r|s|t|u|v|w|x|y|z|\(|\)|\?|:|\||\*)*`

This pattern would match the subject character by character. Each character in the subject is one of the alternatives. The `*` would match all characters.

But wait, the pattern itself contains `(?:` which includes `(`, `?`, `:`. These are in the alternatives. And the pattern contains `|` which is in the alternatives. And `*` which is in the alternatives. And `)` which is in the alternatives.

So the pattern would match itself character by character. Each repetition creates a frame.

Let me test this.
